editorial.headline: Collection Agency Activity: A Clear Path for Foreign Investors in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers collecting claim payments and remitting them to clients, with full foreign ownership permitted nationally and PT PMA registration available in Bali.
editorial.body:
Collection-agency activity is modestly titled but operationally exact: it covers collecting payment on claims and passing the collected payments on to clients. That includes bill- or debt-collection services. The recorded scope describes a payment-recovery and remittance function, rather than simply an administrative back office. Its commercial centre is the handling of money due and the delivery of recovered sums to the client that engaged the service.

Registration is open across the recorded Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales. That range gives the activity a broad formal landing place, but it should not be read as a description of how any particular firm must organise itself: the record establishes only the scales available for this activity. Nationally, its status is TERBUKA and foreign ownership may reach 100%. This is the clear national position: the record sets no foreign-ownership ceiling below full ownership.

In Bali, the conclusion remains positive, with a specific reason. The activity is recorded as open in Bali with high risk, and a PT PMA can register it there. Its Besar scale is classed as Tinggi; that classification lets it survive the provincial moratorium. The moratorium is permanent and island-wide, but the record states that it blocks only low- and medium-low-risk KBLI for PMA. This activity’s Bali position is therefore not an assumption that the restriction is ignored; it is an express consequence of the recorded high-risk Besar-scale treatment.

For founders, the useful reading is direct. The business may be structured around collecting claim payments and transmitting those collected payments to its clients, including bill and debt collection work. It is available at the three recorded scales, open nationally to foreign ownership up to the recorded ceiling, and registrable in Bali through a PT PMA under its recorded Bali treatment. The relevant provincial framework is the permanent, island-wide moratorium cited in the record; its consequence here follows from the recorded high-risk Besar-scale classification.
